chunk:lec01:s1-1: {"heading": "Markov decision processes", "body": [{"type": "prose", "text": "Sequential decision making starts with a Markov decision process. An MDP is fully specified by four ingredients; the Bellman equation later in the lecture is nothing more than these four written down recursively."}, {"type": "bullet_list", "items": [{"text": "States $s \\in S$ — everything the agent needs to know right now", "children": []}, {"text": "Actions $a \\in A$ — the choices available in each state", "children": []}, {"text": "Reward $R(s, a)$ — a number received for taking $a$ in $s$", "children": [{"text": "Immediate and given; not to be confused with value", "children": []}]}, {"text": "Transition function $T(s, a, s')$ — where you land after each action", "children": []}, {"text": "Discount factor $\\gamma \\in [0, 1)$ — how much later rewards count", "children": [{"text": "$\\gamma \\to 0$: myopic, only the next reward counts", "children": []}, {"text": "$\\gamma \\to 1$: far-sighted, but sums may diverge", "children": []}]}]}, {"type": "definition", "term": "Markov property", "definition": "The next state depends only on the current state and action, not on the history that led there."}, {"type": "callout", "kind": "PITFALL", "text": "Reward vs value: the reward is the number you get right now; the value is the total discounted reward you expect from here on. Students mix these up every year."}], "cards": [{"front": "What are the four ingredients of an MDP?", "back": "States, actions, rewards, and a transition function.", "tags": ["mdp"]}, {"front": "What does the discount factor gamma control?", "back": "How much later rewards count relative to immediate ones.", "tags": ["mdp", "discounting"]}]}
chunk:lec01:t151: {"heading": "Board work: the reroll game", "body": [{"type": "prose", "text": "Away from the slides: roll a fair six-sided die and receive the face value in dollars. The game is worth its expected payout, 3.5, so paying anything less is a bargain."}, {"type": "prose", "text": "Now allow one reroll. The trick is to value the second roll first, because its worth is already known: keep the first roll only if it beats 3.5, i.e. a 4, 5 or 6."}, {"type": "equation", "latex": "\\mathbb{E}[\\text{reroll game}] = \\tfrac{1}{2}\\cdot\\tfrac{4+5+6}{3} + \\tfrac{1}{2}\\cdot 3.5 = 4.25", "label": "reroll-value"}, {"type": "callout", "kind": "ASIDE", "text": "This is dynamic programming in miniature: solve the last decision first, then use its value to make the earlier one. The same idea drives value iteration."}], "cards": [{"front": "With one optional reroll of a fair die, which first rolls do you keep?", "back": "4, 5 or 6 — anything that beats the 3.5 expected value of rerolling.", "tags": ["dynamic-programming"]}]}
chunk:lec01:s2-2: {"heading": "The Bellman equation", "body": [{"type": "prose", "text": "The value of a state is the immediate reward plus gamma times the expected value of wherever you land next. The equation is recursive: the value on the left shows up again on the right-hand side."}, {"type": "equation", "latex": "V(s) = \\max_a \\Big[ R(s, a) + \\gamma \\sum_{s'} T(s, a, s')\\, V(s') \\Big]", "label": "bellman"}, {"type": "table", "header": ["Term", "Meaning"], "rows": [["$V(s)$", "value of state $s$"], ["$\\max_a$", "best action available"], ["$\\sum_{s'} T(s, a, s')$", "expectation over next states"], ["$\\gamma$", "discount factor"]]}, {"type": "callout", "kind": "EXAM", "text": "Write the Bellman equation down properly, with the max over actions and the sum over next states. This will be on the exam."}, {"type": "quote", "text": "Once you believe the Bellman equation has a unique fixed point, everything else in this lecture follows.", "attribution": "Lecturer, on the principle of optimality"}], "cards": [{"front": "State the Bellman optimality equation for $V(s)$.", "back": "$V(s) = \\max_a \\Big[ R(s, a) + \\gamma \\sum_{s'} T(s, a, s')\\, V(s') \\Big]$", "tags": ["bellman", "exam"]}, {"front": "Why is the Bellman equation called recursive?", "back": "The value function $V$ appears on both sides of the equation.", "tags": ["bellman"]}]}
synthesis:lec01: {"title": "MDPs and the Bellman Equation", "overview": "Introduces Markov decision processes, derives the Bellman optimality equation from their four ingredients, and turns it into the value iteration algorithm. A board-work detour on a dice game motivates solving the last decision first.", "objectives": ["Name the four ingredients of an MDP and the role of the discount factor.", "Write the Bellman optimality equation and explain why it is recursive.", "Run one sweep of value iteration by hand and state its stopping rule."], "glossary": [{"type": "definition", "term": "Discount factor", "definition": "$\\gamma \\in [0, 1)$; weights a reward $k$ steps ahead by $\\gamma^k$."}, {"type": "definition", "term": "Value function", "definition": "$V(s)$: the expected total discounted reward starting from state $s$ and acting optimally."}, {"type": "definition", "term": "Greedy policy", "definition": "The policy that picks, in every state, the action maximising the Bellman bracket."}], "open_questions": ["Why does the Bellman equation have exactly one fixed point for gamma < 1?", "How many sweeps does value iteration need to reach a given epsilon?"]}
